title: Foundation prepare-before-launch workspace lifecycle
description: Objective: compose the server-owned workspace authorities into the real Foundation service at the only safe point: after reservation/replay discrimination and before physical provider launch. Hard dependencies: task-a3e8a02ddb864c689ac66de7b66bfceb DONE plus task-4af0e3dcc4ad41ea85d409ca0101b11d (host catalog), task-a500fef07e1f4b1aae8d810633a4763d (worktree materializer), task-e7a40bc0324749df8afbf45c8c8a180b (workspace capture), and task-6109b2f4306c4b00a6ecdb74074129c4 (capture-context ledger) DONE. Deliverable: a daemon lifecycle port/factory wired by createStoreDependencies/createDaemonCommandPorts and createFoundationDispatchHandler. For a fresh reservation it resolves durable catalog authority, materializes the exact detached attempt worktree, invokes the existing Foundation input hydrator over catalog scopes and real observers, proves caller base/input/cwd proposals agree, scans and commits the clean durable prelaunch capture context, then launches only in that assigned root. The service carries the derived captureRef lexically into captureResult; replay returns before any new scan/launch; only a durably PROVEN capture may identity-fenced release the worktree. Missing or unverifiable authority fails closed and launches zero processes. NOT in scope: implementing captureResult's postlaunch producer (parent task), server-owned argv/model/limit selection (task-9a1eb61d), graph fan-out, verification/review, or final acceptance. Owned paths (10 maximum): apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-capture-lifecycle.ts/.js/.test.ts, work/foundation-attempt-service.ts/.test.ts, daemon-foundation-command.ts, daemon-command-registry.ts/.test.ts, daemon-store-dependencies.ts/.test.ts. Verification command: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck; $a=$LASTEXITCODE; pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test; $b=$LASTEXITCODE; pnpm --filter @moe/runner test; $c=$LASTEXITCODE; Write-Host "DAEMON_TC=$a DAEMON_TEST=$b RUNNER_TEST=$c"; if ($a -ne 0 -or $b -ne 0 -or $c -ne 0) { exit 1 }`, and both test legs must print nonzero counts.
definitionOfDone: The production store provider accepts an optional bounded Foundation workspace catalog path outside the request plane, loads/decodes it through task-4af0e3d's authority, and wires catalog/materializer/hydrator/scanner/context-ledger dependencies through createDaemonCommandPorts to the real foundation.dispatch handler; absent/unreadable/invalid configuration refuses only Foundation workspace preparation with exact code/layer and leaves every pre-existing command path byte-identical.

For a NEW durable reservation, createFoundationAttemptService invokes required prepareCapture exactly once before launch: it resolves the final durable RepositoryObservation, creates/adopts the derived detached worktree at its base, hydrates actual input bytes under catalog scopes, proves request base/input/cwd proposals agree, captures the clean baseline, and commits a FoundationCaptureContext before any provider process starts.

A caller cwd or input entry never becomes authority: launch always uses the committed assigned worktree and hydrated manifest; a conflicting proposal refuses FOUNDATION_CAPTURE_WORKSPACE_MISMATCH at DAEMON_FOUNDATION_CAPTURE, records the unproven attempt under that exact code/layer, invokes zero launch/capture calls, and leaves no unowned worktree residue.

Replay returns the original durable result or exact in-progress/suspect refusal before resolving, materializing, hydrating, preparing, or launching again; preparation replay is byte-identical, conflicting context is preserved/refused, and two deferred parallel dispatches prove their immutable captureRefs and worktrees cannot cross.

Only after a proven launch observation does the service call captureResult with the derived captureRef plus existing attempt/base/node/observation/session facts; capture/context refusal or callback failure stays UNKNOWN under the deciding exact code/layer. A proven durable result identity-fenced releases its worktree, while unproven/uncertain settlement retains or quarantines it for reconciliation.

Focused real-store and real-temp-Git tests drive the production provider/registry/service path, assert exact code and refusing layer plus raw event/decision/process counts and a nonzero generated hostile roster, and include accepted, missing-config, mismatch, replay, crash-window, and concurrent isolation controls; mutations moving prepare after launch or swapping captureRefs redden named tests.

Every pre-existing registered kind remains on its unchanged handler path and the exact registry roster stays closed; daemon typecheck/test and runner test exit 0 with printed nonzero counts, new bridge plain-Node loads, and each production source targets <=250 lines and stays below 400.
taskRails: Preparation order is a security property: durable reservation/replay discrimination -> server workspace resolution/materialization/hydration/baseline/context commit -> physical launch -> postlaunch capture. Never move a step across those boundaries.
Request launchTemplate.cwd and inputManifest are conflict proposals only. They can cause a mismatch refusal but can never select the worktree, scope, or sealed input used for launch/capture.
No module-global mutable context or map; each dispatch carries one immutable durable captureRef in lexical state, and parallel attempts must remain isolated.
Do not absorb task-9a1eb61d's argv/launchSelection/limits work or the parent task's postlaunch producer; preserve upstream runner/daemon refusal code and layer verbatim.

Instead the fixture now configures a real catalog through `workspaceCatalogPath`. That also closes the gap I disclosed at step-6: this is now the ONLY place where the whole provider -> registry -> command -> service wiring is exercised by production code end to end.

Authored-path splitting is still covered by the runner's own workspace-manifest suite and by `persists result-manifest identity` in the sibling suite, which kept its own scope-shaped fixture — but the proven Windows journey no longer exercises it, and that is a real reduction rather than a neutral edit.

qa-bbdecc14 — sharpening my own rejection issue 1 before you build against it. Two additions from peer review of the verdict; both make the new test harder to fake. The rejection text stands, this only tightens it.

1. DISTINCT IS NOT ENOUGH — THE SWAP SURVIVES IT. `refs.size === 2` passes a variant that hands each arm the OTHER arm's ref. Assert positively, per arm: each returned captureRef equals `deriveFoundationCaptureRef` of ITS OWN slot, not merely that the two differ. The lifecycle test already does exactly this one layer down (`first.captureRef).toBe(deriveFoundationCaptureRef(slotOf(left)))` and the same for right) — lift that shape, not just the `.not.toBe`.

2. ASSERT THE WORKTREE AT THE DISPATCH LAYER TOO. My mutant rebuilt `prepared` from the first-seen ref, which crosses BOTH ref and root together. A narrower mutant that shares only the worktree while keeping refs distinct would survive a refs-only test. So assert distinct `assignment.realWorktreePath` per arm as well, and that each durable context read back by captureRef carries its own root — same cross-assert the lifecycle test makes.

3. RUN THE DRILL BOTH WAYS. Per my issue 3: after the fix, re-run the module-level `stickyRef` mutant in `foundation-attempt-service.ts` (~:231) with `--test-name-pattern` on the new case AND in the whole-file run. A kill that only appears in isolation is not a kill in the gate. The whole-file run is the authority; the focused run only locates.

Do not take the shape on faith — re-run the mutant. I will re-run it myself at review, plus the prepare-after-launch drill and the full recorded gate.

Also: sha256 fixture repo, `core.autocrlf=false`, bind_repository before activate, and a second activation means a second real worktree that must also be released. That is the honest cost of this fix; it is not a one-liner, and I am not grading it as one.
